## Triage verdict — Phase 3 scope confirmed, gate NOT met, audit deferred

**Scope confirmed against current main** (`origin/main` 9f730f1c2, verified 2026-11-02):

- `ReplicationTracker::accept` still checks only the upper bound — `if envelope.header_version > MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION` (`pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs:712`) — so the Phase 1 (#4471) v0-admission gap is still present; no lower-bound check.
- The Snapshot arm still assigns `self.header_version = envelope.header_version` unconditionally (`replication.rs:752`, guarded only by `cursor_before == base-for-snapshot-version`) — so the Phase 2 (#4487) rollback gap is still present; no `HeaderVersionRegressed` variant exists anywhere in the file.
- The Phase 3 deliverables are absent as expected: no contract statement ("a frame is admitted only if…") in the `replication.rs` module doc (module doc at `:1-51` is the F12.13 envelope/cursor contract only), no cross-reference from the `accept` doc comment, and `ReplicationTracker::new` (`:673-681`) performs no range check and carries no inert-tracker doc.
- The landed payload-side legs are present as cited: `validate_payload_journal_header` and `chain_payload` in the accept path; #4486 is CLOSED. They are the embodiment legs, not phases — no action.
- Packet note: the design-doc path in the packet (`files/designs/code-id-replication-admission.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy workspace) does not resolve in the current workspace checkout — only signal state under `hidden_files/` is present. Triage used the full design body on #4592 (which contains the contract, decisions 1–4, and the (a)–(d) disposition list) as the source of truth. No packet defect filed: the design content itself is intact on the issue.

**Gating recorded — audit must NOT start:**

- Phase 1 (#4471, envelope range): OPEN, `status/in-progress`, `queue/claimed` + `work/assigned` — not landed.
- Phase 2 (#4487, snapshot monotonicity): OPEN, `queue/queued` — not landed.
- The Phase 1–2 gate for this audit has therefore NOT cleared. This issue correctly carries `status/blocked` and keeps it until both land.

**Follow-up:** the implementation packet (contract statement in module doc + restore-precondition inventory with required dispositions (a)–(d), acceptance criteria intact per this issue) is **deferred, not enqueued**, until #4471 and #4487 both land — enqueuing now would create work that must immediately park against this same gate, and the task brief forbids starting the audit before the gates clear. Whoever closes the second of #4471/#4487 (or the next triage sweep seeing both CLOSED) should enqueue the Phase 3 implementation packet from this issue's acceptance criteria unchanged.

No code touched in this triage task.

## Current triage — 2026-11-04

**#4593 remains live and gated; it is not superseded.** Rechecked against current main at [707689e32d1d](https://github.com/developing-today/code/commit/707689e32d1edde036e2e3ab989a3fb0040dddd3).

- **Phase 1 gate is clear.** [#4471 is closed](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/4471) and its fix PR #4540 is merged. At current main, ReplicationTracker::new rejects header versions outside the restore range ([replication.rs:671–682](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/707689e32d1edde036e2e3ab989a3fb0040dddd3/pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs#L671-L682)), and accept applies the range check to incoming envelopes ([replication.rs:720–729](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/707689e32d1edde036e2e3ab989a3fb0040dddd3/pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs#L720-L729)).
- **Phase 2 gate is not clear.** [#4487 remains open](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/4487); fix [PR #4808](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4808) is still open (2/2 checks passing, merge-ready, but not landed). On current main, the Snapshot arm checks the snapshot base, then updates self.cursor and self.header_version without a lower-version guard ([replication.rs:749–765](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/707689e32d1edde036e2e3ab989a3fb0040dddd3/pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs#L749-L765)). The PR’s green checks do not satisfy the explicit “land Phases 1–2 first” gate.

**Current blocker:** Phase 2 (#4487 / PR #4808) must land on main before this closing audit starts.

**Ordering:** land #4808; then re-run Phase 3 from the resulting current main, complete the required dispositions (a)–(d), publish the contract and per-precondition inventory here, and run the acceptance test per this issue. If #4808 closes without landing, re-check the gate rather than treating Phase 2 as complete. No Phase 3 code or audit work was started in this triage.

### Required dispositions

**(a) Entry-kind version gating — CONFIRMED GAP, filed as #7970.** Yes: a signed in-range snapshot can carry e.g. an `ExecutionProfile` entry (requires version 2, or 4 with a persisted budget) on a version-1 header. `accept` admits it (decodability is the only per-entry check), the verified cursor advances, and the durable receiver commits it — then restore refuses the journal whole (`core.rs:562-565`). No state a real v1 journal could never hold is ever *applied*, because restore's check runs before the entry is applied and its refusal is total; the defect is admission: the replica commits a chain it cannot restore, the same brick-at-next-open shape Phase 1 closed for version-0 envelopes (see the comment at `replication.rs:740-744`). Filed, not fixed here, per this issue's scope.

**(b) Session-bootstrap version source — decision 2's property holds, in a stronger form than the design recorded.** The only production construction site is `ReplicationReceiver::begin_session` (`replication_receiver.rs:277`), which passes the receiver's stored version: at `open` it comes from `validate_committed_journal` over the committed replica journal (`replication_receiver.rs:522`; its header range check at line 550), defaults to `JOURNAL_VERSION` before the first commit, and is updated at every Terminal commit from the committing tracker's version. The landed Phase 1 took the fallible-constructor ending the design listed as the alternative: `ReplicationTracker::new` itself returns `UnsupportedJournalVersion` for an out-of-range version (`replication.rs:698`), and `begin_session` maps that to *no session*, so every frame is refused with `NoSession` (comment at `replication_receiver.rs:278-281`) — an out-of-range tracker cannot exist at this call site, let alone accept frames. Cross-session monotonicity: a new session's tracker is seeded from the **committed** version only, and a snapshot below it is refused (see the snapshot-regression evidence in row 3 / disposition (c) discussion), so no committed chain ever moves backward. A new session *can* start below a previous session's **uncommitted** progress — staged bytes are discarded on abort/reconnect (`abort_session`, `begin_session`) and never became replica state, so nothing durable regresses.

**(c) Pre-fix terminal hygiene — CONFIRMED COVERED.** Two independent reasons: (i) `accept` range-checks the envelope before the kind match (`replication.rs:745`), so an out-of-range Terminal is refused whatever the tracker's version; (ii) no post-fix tracker can hold an out-of-range version at all — construction refuses it (`replication.rs:698`) and the receiver's stored version is range-checked at open (`replication_receiver.rs:550`). A tracker whose version was set by a pre-Phase-1 snapshot therefore cannot persist into a post-fix binary. Evidence: test `signed_v0_frames_are_refused_without_advancing_tracker_state` covers Snapshot, Tail **and Terminal** v0 frames, state untouched, plus a control frame chaining afterwards; `tracker_requires_a_supported_starting_header_version` covers construction. Snapshot regression itself is refused at `replication.rs:780` (test `snapshot_refuses_a_header_version_downgrade`).

**(d) Second doors — dispositioned, no competing frame door.** (i) `ReplicationReceiver::accept_frame` pre-decodes the first frame (`replication_receiver.rs:324`) only to enforce snapshot-first session ordering (`SessionMustStartWithSnapshot`); it performs **no** version validation, and a decode failure falls through to `tracker.accept`, which refuses with `MalformedFrame`. Named exception: ordering, not admission; all version checks delegate to `accept`. (ii) `validate_committed_journal` (`replication_receiver.rs:522`) and the replica parse validator (`world/replica.rs`, header check at line ~130) validate the **stored journal's** header at open — world, range (as version == 0 or > MAX, equivalent to `check_journal_version` while `JOURNAL_VERSION` = 1), single header, decodability. They are the bootstrap sources for (b), not frame paths: no frame reaches a journal except through `accept` plus a Terminal commit. Disposition: delegated-equivalent. (iii) The writer feed (`world_replication_net.rs:146-274`) reads its own journal's header version to build envelopes — producer side, not a receiver door; its source journal was range-checked when the writer restored it. Named exception. (iv) `world_doctor.rs` version checks are diagnostics only, not on any accept path.

### Divergences from design #4592's recorded decisions (noted, not gaps)

- Decision 2 offered two endings for `ReplicationTracker::new`; the design recorded the inert-tracker ending, but the landed Phase 1 took the **fallible constructor** (see (b)). The safety property the design wanted holds a fortiori.
- Decision 3 asked for a dedicated `HeaderVersionRegressed` variant; the landed Phase 2 refuses a snapshot downgrade with the existing `HeaderVersionChanged` (`replication.rs:780`, comment citing #4487; test `snapshot_refuses_a_header_version_downgrade`). Refusal semantics are identical; only error-variant diagnosability differs from the design text.
